headline: Egypt reach World Cup knockout stage for first time
summary: Despite Mohamed Salah's early substitution in a 1-1 draw with Iran, Egypt's evolving attack secures a historic spot in the round-of-32.
details: Egypt has reached the World Cup knockout stage for the first time in its history after finishing second in Group G.
In their final group game against Iran in Seattle, the match ended in a 1-1 draw with midfielder Mahmoud Saber scoring for Egypt inside five minutes.
Talismanic forward Mohamed Salah had a quiet game and left the field in the 57th minute after asking to be substituted. Coach Hossam Hassan stated he does not believe the issue is serious.
Salah remains the centerpiece of the attack, having scored one goal and provided two assists in the group stage, while tallying nine of Egypt's 20 goals during the qualifying campaign.
Under coach Hassan, Egypt has adopted a more dynamic style, utilizing Salah's presence to create space for teammates like Emam Ashour, Trezeguet, and Zico.
Egypt narrowly missed out on the top spot in the group on goal difference after Belgium thrashed New Zealand 5-1.
The team will now face Australia in the round-of-32 match on July 3 in Dallas.
caption:
A historic first for Egypt! 🇪🇬

They've officially reached the World Cup knockout stage for the first time ever.

Egypt has reached the World Cup knockout stage for the first time in its history after finishing second in Group G.

In their final group game against Iran in Seattle, the match ended in a 1-1 draw with midfielder Mahmoud Saber scoring for Egypt inside five minutes.

Talismanic forward Mohamed Salah had a quiet game and left the field in the 57th minute after asking to be substituted. Coach Hossam Hassan stated he does not believe the issue is serious.

Salah remains the centerpiece of the attack, having scored one goal and provided two assists in the group stage, while tallying nine of Egypt's 20 goals during the qualifying campaign.

Under coach Hassan, Egypt has adopted a more dynamic style, utilizing Salah's presence to create space for teammates like Emam Ashour, Trezeguet, and Zico.

Egypt narrowly missed out on the top spot in the group on goal difference after Belgium thrashed New Zealand 5-1.

The team will now face Australia in the round-of-32 match on July 3 in Dallas.

caption:
Injury scare for Mohamed Salah! 🇪🇬

The Egyptian star was forced off the pitch during their World Cup draw with Iran.

Egypt's Mohamed Salah left the field in the 57th minute of Friday's 1-1 draw against Iran in Seattle, after asking to be substituted due to an injury.

The 34-year-old winger, who has scored one goal and provided two assists in the group stage, will be assessed to determine his availability for the round-of-32 match against Australia.

Coach Hossam Hassan stated that he does not believe the injury is serious, as Egypt prepares for their knockout stage game on July 3 in Dallas.

Despite the injury scare, Egypt has reached the World Cup knockout stage for the first time in their history.

Salah remains the centerpiece of the attack, having scored nine of Egypt's 20 goals during the World Cup qualifying campaign.

Under coach Hassan, Egypt has played more dynamically, utilizing Salah's presence to create space for teammates like Emam Ashour, Trezeguet, and Zico.

Egypt finished second in Group G after Belgium thrashed New Zealand 5-1, denying Egypt the top spot on goal difference.
